$comment: The app's custom menu items, in one place, read by BOTH languages: Rust builds the
menu from it (build_menu in src-tauri/src/lib.rs, via include_str! + serde) and
TypeScript both handles the events it implies (src/actions.ts) and documents its
accelerators (src/shortcuts.ts). Every item used to be written out four times — a
MenuItemBuilder in Rust, a match arm on its id, the `menu-{id}` string that arm
emitted, and the listener for that same string in main.ts — plus a fifth time as
prose in the shortcuts sheet. Getting the prefix or the id wrong in any one of those
places failed SILENTLY: no compile error, no runtime error, the menu item just did
nothing when clicked. There is nothing left to get out of sync here.
PREDEFINED ITEMS ARE NOT LISTED HERE, on purpose. Cut/Copy/Paste, About, Services,
Hide, Minimize, Zoom and everything macOS appends to the Window menu are routed by
the OS through the responder chain to whichever window is focused, with no app code
involved at all — they have no id to dispatch and no event to listen for. This file
covers the custom items, which are exactly the ones this app has to route itself.
The menu stays BUILT IN RUST. This manifest moves the strings, not the construction:
a JS-built menu's action callback runs in the webview that built the menu, so with
several windows open File > Save would save the wrong document (design note 1 in
README.md). Adding an item here does not make it a frontend concern.
Fields:
id                the menu item's id; the event it dispatches is `menu-{id}`
label             what the menu draws
accelerator       Tauri accelerator string, omitted for menu-only items
submenu           which submenu below it belongs to
separatorBefore   draw a separator above this item (menu grouping is data too)
description       what it does, in the Help > Keyboard Shortcuts sheet's voice
`description` is required even for items with no accelerator, which the sheet
therefore never shows. It is the one-line answer to 'what does this item do', which
is worth having written down next to the item either way, and it means adding an
accelerator later is a one-field change rather than a hunt for wording.
